subject: KlytnPharma private deployment — connectivity sprint and access matrix
messages:
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Reed <olivia.reed@klytnpharma.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: KlytnPharma private deployment — connectivity sprint and access matrix

Hi Olivia —

Great to kick this off. Per our call, attached is a lightweight access matrix (access_matrix_klytn_v1.xlsx) and a first-pass network topology (network_topology_draft.pdf). Proposed agenda for initial sprint:

- Network clearance: VPC peering, private endpoints, and IP allowlist
- Firewall rule review and egress constraints
- On-prem package install requirements and physical handoff window
- Key management and KMS/HSM routing (high level)
- Acceptance criteria and go/no-go checkpoints

Can you confirm the following by EOD Wednesday so we can lock the sprint dates?
1) Primary point of contact for infrastructure (name + email)
2) CIDR blocks you plan to use for the peering and any NATed ranges
3) Whether you prefer VPN or Direct Connect-equivalent (we can support both)

I've copied Monica and Irene from our implementations and networking teams — Monica will run the integration sprint, Irene will own the secure-connect handoff and audit artifacts.

Next steps on our side once we have the details: we will populate the access matrix with required accounts, user roles, and required outbound IPs; draft firewall rule CSV for your ops; and schedule a 60-minute tech walkthrough.

Attachments: access_matrix_klytn_v1.xlsx, network_topology_draft.pdf

Thanks —
Ethan Park
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
ethan.park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

---
Redwood Inference — production inference for regulated workloads

From: Olivia Reed <olivia.reed@klytnpharma.com>

Cc: IT Ops <itops@klytnpharma.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KlytnPharma private deployment — connectivity sprint and access matrix

Thanks Ethan — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Primary infra contact: Marcus Lane (marcus.lane@klytnpharma.com), CCed our IT Ops alias for visibility.
- CIDR plan: We will use 10.40.0.0/16 for the application VPC and 10.41.0.0/16 for the management VPC.
- Connectivity: we prefer an IPsec VPN to start, but we may upgrade to a private interconnect later in Q3.

Security notes / asks:
- Klytn is SOC2 Type II; we need a short list of what audit evidence you will provide post-install (logs, access records, key rotation proof).
- We require that any outbound egress to public internet from the appliance be restricted; can you include suggested egress ACLs?

For scheduling: Marcus is available next Tue/Thu mornings. Can you share a slot?

Olivia Reed
Head of IT, KlytnPharma
olivia.reed@klytnpharma.com

Ethan / Irene — quick sync items from implementation planning perspective: 

1) I'll own the sprint schedule and runbook. Proposed sprint window: Apr 2 — Apr 6 (5 business days). Prep week: Mar 26 — Mar 30.
2) I'll populate the access_matrix_klytn_v1.xlsx with roles: deploy-admin, net-admin, sec-audit, app-svc. Irene — please add the exact artifacts we'll collect for audit (log retention, token rotation proof, trace ids).
3) Firewall rules: I propose we send a preliminary fw_rules_proposal.csv to Klytn that lists ports and destinations rather than appliance IPs (so their security team can validate quickly). Once they confirm CIDRs we swap concrete IPs.

Irene: can you confirm who on security will sign off on the audit checklist? Also, do we have a standard DocuSign template for private peering agreements or should I draft one from the playbook link?

I can take the Tuesday morning slot (Apr 3, 09:00 PT) for the tech walkthrough — I'll send a calendar invite once Olivia confirms Marcus.

Hi all —

This is the ClearRoute networks team — thanks for looping us in. Attached is a short CSV with our recommended border ACLs (fw_rules_proposal.csv) and the public-facing peering IP block we will advertise if you choose managed peering.

Peering notes: 
- Proposed peering IPs: 198.51.100.240/28 (we will assign host IPs during the handoff)
- We support BGP if Klytn wants dynamic routing; otherwise static routes are fine for the initial VPN.
- We require a contact for change windows — we recommend two 2-hour maintenance windows during the ops week for BGP session setup and validation.

If you need a ticket for IP whitelisting to your internal firewall, let us know and we'll open it now.

Regards,
ClearRoute NetOps

Olivia / Marcus / team — thanks for the fast responses. Summary and agreed next steps below:

- Connectivity: start with IPsec VPN; we will keep the BGP option in scope for a Q3 interconnect upgrade. ClearRoute will provide peering IPs and can support BGP if needed.
- Action items (owners & due dates):
  * Klytn: confirm NATed ranges and any downstream ACLs by Mar 23 (owner: Marcus Lane)
  * ClearRoute: open ticket and confirm assigned peering IPs + maintenance windows by Mar 24 (owner: ClearRoute NetOps)
  * Redwood (Monica): finalize fw_rules_proposal.csv and pre-populate access_matrix_klytn_v1.xlsx by Mar 25
  * Redwood (Irene): prepare audit artifacts checklist and DocuSign peering agreement by Mar 26

I've uploaded the working docs to the shared onboarding folder: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/impl/KL-2028-007/onboarding-playbook and started a DocuSign envelope (link below) for the peering agreement so legal can get ahead of it: https://docusign.net/KL-2028-007/peering-agreement

If there are any blockers from security or procurement, flag them to me directly and we'll escalate to the right owners. Looking forward to getting this into staging.

Thanks —
Ethan
